newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm at open in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm at open in thin dealings.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firm on Wednesday but trading remained thin with investors mostly absent from the market.
Dealers said the firm close of Wall Street stocks and the decision by the Federal Reserve to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged overnight had a muted impact on the market.
"The market opened a bit better but there is really not much interest. Those who are not on holiday are busying with other Christmas things," said a dealer with a local firm.
At 0120 GMT, the Straits Times Industrial index is up 6.50 points to 2,183.02.

Volume was a light 12.97 million units with 110 gainers against 39 losers. Property group Wing Tai saw several block trades crossed at between S$3.89 to S$3.90. Times Publications also saw a block deal of 710,000 shares at S$3.00.

Retailer Hour Glass shares slumped 8.26 percent to S$1.00, down nine cents from its previous close with 209,000 shares traded. Analysts blamed the company's shock 49.7 percent plunge in interim profits to S$2.54 million.
Among the early gainers were DBS foreign, Singapore Press foreign and Cerebos Pacific rising between 30 and 20 cents each.
